transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Well, I came in today because I've started to feel... I suppose in a quiet but stubborn sort of way, that the best version of my life is just behind me. It feels like no matter what I do, no amount of planning or discipline is going to get me back to feeling like myself again.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Well, this has been going on since a hiking injury I had a little over three years ago. Let's see... it's been about three years and three months now.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before the injury?

I suppose I do, yes. I haven't really noticed a change there. I mean, I still enjoy reading a good book, and I like catching up with my friends when we get together. So... no, I wouldn't say I've stopped enjoying my usual activities. It's really just that underlying feeling I mentioned.
Would you say this feeling of your life being behind you is something that mildly bothers you or significantly interferes with your daily life?

Well, I suppose it's somewhere in between. I still manage all the basics at home without any real trouble, so it hasn't completely stopped me in my tracks. But... I have definitely stepped back from quite a few things. 

I used to be fairly involved in mentoring, and I'd regularly go out to community events or music gatherings. Lately, I've just let those go. I haven't been making any travel plans, either. So while I'm still functioning fine day-to-day, my weeks are just... well, they're much smaller than they used to be.
Do you feel like you're getting as much pleasure out of the things you enjoy as you used to?

I think so, yes. I'd say the amount of pleasure is about the same. Like I mentioned, when I sit down with a book or actually get together with friends, I still really enjoy it. It doesn't feel diminished or muted at all. It's just... well, I'm doing fewer things overall, but the things I do still feel just as good to me.
Do you often feel sad, empty, or hopeless?

Well, I wouldn't say I'm in tears most days, or that it's anything dramatic. But... there is definitely this low, gray tone running underneath everything. It's just sort of there, even when I'm in the studio or sitting across from my wife at dinner. It's not a sharp sadness, just a constant, quiet emptiness, I suppose.
Would you say this feeling of emptiness and the changes in your life are affecting your relationships with others, such as your wife?

I don't really think so. My wife and I have a pretty steady routine, and this hasn't caused any real friction between us. I mean, she obviously knows I'm staying in more these days, but we still talk and spend time together just fine. 

As for other people... well, I'm seeing them less simply because I dropped out of those community events. But when I do see my friends, everything feels completely normal. So, no, I wouldn't say it's hurting my relationships.
Would you describe your current feelings of emptiness and low mood as mildly bothersome or quite distressing?

I'd say it's mildly bothersome. It's not something that's tearing me apart or making me feel distressed, really. It's just... well, it's just there. It's more of a nuisance, this constant low feeling, rather than something that's overwhelming me.
How long have you been feeling this low, gray tone and emptiness?

It's been quite a while now. It really started after a hiking injury I had... that was a little over three years ago. If I think about the exact timing, it's been about three years and three months now.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since you started feeling this way?

No, I haven't really noticed any big changes there. My appetite is about the same as it's always been, and I'm eating normally. As for sleep, I still get my usual seven or eight hours a night. So, no, nothing different in those areas.
Would you say this low, gray tone and emptiness you're feeling is something you can't stop thinking about, or is it more in the background of your daily thoughts?

It's definitely more in the background. I mean, I don't sit around dwelling on it all day or anything like that. It's just... well, it's always kind of there while I'm going about my day. I certainly wouldn't say I can't stop thinking about it, no.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt better and this low, gray tone lifted?
No, not really. I mean, I might have a decent afternoon here or there, but... no, I haven't had a stretch of two weeks where it completely went away. It's just been pretty steady since it started.
Have you experienced any thoughts of death or suicide since you started feeling this low, gray tone?

No, I haven't. I mean, I feel low, sure, but I don't have any thoughts about dying or hurting myself. Nothing like that at all. It's just a... a persistent dullness, really. But no suicidal thoughts, no.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or making decisions since you started feeling this way?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues with that. My focus seems to be fine. I can still sit down and read, or figure out what I need to get done around the house without any trouble. Making decisions hasn't been a problem either. So, no, I wouldn't say I've had any difficulty concentrating.
Would you say this low, gray tone and emptiness are affecting your interest in social activities most of the day?

No, I wouldn't say that. I still keep up with my friends and... well, I still go out and see family. The low feeling is always there in the background, but it doesn't really stop me from wanting to be around people or doing things socially. I still participate just fine.
Would you say this feeling of emptiness and low mood is something that you think about every day?

No, I wouldn't say I actually think about it every day. It's not really something I dwell on. Like I mentioned, it's more just... a feeling that's always there in the background. I don't wake up and focus my thoughts on being low or empty. I just go about my normal day, read, do what I need to do, and it's just sort of present. But no, I'm not actively thinking about the mood itself on a daily basis.
Would you say this low, gray tone and emptiness are significantly impacting your daily functioning, or is it more of a mild impairment?

I'd say it's more of a mild impairment. I mean, I still manage all the basics at home just fine. But... I guess I have stepped back from a lot of other things. I'm not really doing the mentoring I used to do, and I've pulled away from community events and music gatherings. I haven't made any travel plans lately, either. So, I'm functioning, but my weeks are just much smaller than they used to be.
Would you say that this low, gray tone and emptiness have interfered with your ability to work or be productive in any significant way?

No, not really. I'm retired, so I don't have a job to go to anymore. As for being productive at home, I still get the day-to-day chores done without much trouble. I pay the bills, keep the house in order, that sort of thing. The feeling is there, but it hasn't stopped me from taking care of my normal responsibilities.
Do you feel like this low, gray tone and emptiness are worsening over time?
No, I wouldn't say it's worsening. It's... pretty steady, really. I haven't noticed any big shifts where it feels heavier or darker than before. It just stays at that same level, day in and day out.
Would you say that most days, you feel more than half of the day is spent feeling this low, gray tone and emptiness?

I'm not really sure if it's more than half the day, to be honest. I haven't... I haven't exactly kept track of the hours. It's just sort of this constant background feeling. I don't really notice when it starts or stops, so I couldn't tell you for sure how much of the day it actually takes up.
